newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, rally stalls.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, rally stalls.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Wednesday, with the recovery of the past week now seen stalling, analysts said.
"The trade has been buying and trying to run the market back up, but demand has been tailing off in the Far East and the funds are still short," Mitsui & Co USA bullion dealer, Greg Drury, said.
"With the year coming to a close some producers are looking a bit exposed and are waiting for a further bounce to about $385 in cash gold before hedging but they may not get it," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down 30 cents at $383.00, after falling back near the close from the session highs at $384.30
The December 1996/December 1997 gold spread ended little changed around $14.40 an ounce, but the contango had narrowed from around $16.00 in the past month, unnerving some producers, analysts said.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $380.90/381.40 an ounce, against the London Tuesday afternoon fix of $381.50, and the New York close Tuesday at $381.50/382.00.

Earlier the U.S. Labor Department reported the September CPI rose 0.3 percent, producing an annual U.S. CPI inflation rate of 3.0 percent, which was unlikely to provide much of an incentive to buy gold as an inflation hedge, analysts said.
But COMEX gold stocks were down 16,840 ounces at 1,057,338 ounces Tuesday, the lowest level since November 2, 1977.
"This sudden drawdown recently could offer some upside support to gold prices over the next few days," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
COMEX December silver saw a session high at $5.080 an ounce, but was sold sharply near the close, ending down 2.5 cents at $5.020 an ounce.
Major resistance at $5.100 had not been breached during the past week's recovery from a month-long downtrend, analysts said, and momentum indicators were suggesting another slide was likely.

Silver led the decline in precious metals in the past month, analysts noted, and the spot gold/silver ratio ended wider at 76.02 Wednesday, as silver fell, after a decline to 75.4 in the past week, when silver was recovering.
NYMEX January platinum ended down 30 cents at $388.20 an ounce.
But NYMEX December palladium closed up 20 cents at $117.70, after palladium fixed at new three year lows in the bullion market in London earlier this week.

"The weakness in palladium prices is being blamed on numerous factors, including Russian exports, lower use by electronics companies and short selling by commodity funds," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"Fund selling is the most reasonable explanation," he said.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
